project_specification.project_name: nullius — campaign driver gaps (spec D): resume, import-allowlist consistency, runtime-root verification
project_specification.addition_summary: Three gaps left open by specs A to C and SEC-1, each a self-contained change to the orchestrator or its sandbox child: - A campaign cannot be resumed: run_campaign always creates a fresh campaign and plants fresh roots, so a campaign interrupted mid-run restarts from scratch. Add resumption from the existing node rows. - The sandbox child's import allowlist advertises numpy, which the evaluation runtime does not provide, so a signal that imports numpy passes the guard, then fails at runtime, wasting a trial. Make the allowlist match what the runtime can actually import. - GVisorSandbox trusts whatever directory NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT names; a partial or tampered runtime root runs agent code anyway. Have it verify the root against the manifest digest the provisioning script already writes. No new member, no new dependency. Each feature edits one existing source file (plus its test), all in the orchestrator member except the shared sandbox child.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / SQLite or PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions). runsc and bwrap installed; the gVisor runtime root is /opt/nullius/gvisor-runtime with a sibling manifest.
existing_context.test_baseline: Measured 2026-10-06 on main (HEAD 1055aa2): workspace tests/ 1621 passed; orchestrator member suite 362 passed + 5 skipped (serial; the 5 are the real-runsc tests, run only when runsc and NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT are set).
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md. Typed refusals open with a greppable code word in the raising module. Tests never reach the network or read a credential, and must pass under pytest-xdist (no module-level mutable state shared across tests; unique ids per test).
Existing pieces (read; edit only the file a feature names): - orchestrator._campaign.run_campaign(*, campaign_type, workspaces, rounds, width, allowance, author, evaluator, policy, context, sidecar_selection, emit) -> CampaignResult(campaign_id, roots, nodes, rounds_run, stop_reason, manifest). It calls discovery.create_campaign (which mints a new campaign_id), plants one root per workspace with orchestrator._roots.plant_root, seals nulls once with sidecar_selection.persist(campaign_id), evaluates the roots, then runs the round loop until a stop reason. plant_root is idempotent (same values answer the same id), the trial ledger is idempotent per node, and the stores refuse a conflicting rewrite. - orchestrator._sandbox_child.AGENT_IMPORTS_ALLOWLIST (a frozenset) and _TRUSTED_IMPORT_ROOTS both list numpy today. The child runs under the gVisor runtime root (polars, pyarrow, contract, app; no numpy) or, for the unisolated runtime, the host interpreter. - orchestrator._gvisor.GVisorSandbox(*, runsc, runtime_root, state_root, limits=None, lake_roots=()) resolves runsc at construction (_require_runsc) and raises GVisorUnavailableError (code word isolation_required) when it cannot. deploy/gvisor/provision_runtime.sh writes <root>.manifest.json beside the root, carrying tree_sha256 (the sha256 of the sorted per-file sha256 sums of the whole tree), python, polars, pyarrow and built_at. - discovery.create_campaign(campaign_type, workspaces, *, campaign_id=None, database_url=None, env=None); passing an existing campaign_id is how a caller addresses an existing campaign.

category.name: Campaign Driver Gaps
category.feature: System resumes an interrupted campaign with orchestrator._campaign.resume_campaign(campaign_id, *, rounds, width, allowance, author, evaluator, policy, context, emit), and it answers the same CampaignResult run_campaign answers, continuing the existing campaign rather than planting a new one. - It reads the campaign's existing node rows from context.database_url. A campaign_id with no node rows raises CampaignResumeError (code word campaign_resume) naming the id: resume continues work, it does not start it. - It does not call create_campaign, does not plant new roots, and does not re-seal nulls (Type-R sealing is write-once and already done). The roots are the existing depth-0 rows. - Any planted root not yet evaluated (no metrics and no fail_class) is evaluated before the round loop, so a campaign interrupted between planting and evaluating its roots finishes that step on resume. - It then runs the round loop exactly as run_campaign does — the same budget_account over the campaign's own ledger rows, the same policy.select, the same NodeWorker batch with retry_interrupted, the same four stop reasons — and finishes the campaign manifest. Because the child id is uuid5 and the ledger and stores are idempotent, a node already expanded and evaluated is not repeated. - run_campaign is refactored so the shared loop, root-evaluation and finish logic are one private helper both entry points call; its own behaviour, signature and tests are unchanged. - emit receives the same per-node and per-round events, plus one opening event naming the resumed campaign_id and the count of nodes already present. - A test resumes after roots are planted but not evaluated and shows the roots gain metrics. A test resumes mid-campaign and shows the node count grows. A test resumes an unknown campaign_id and shows it raises CampaignResumeError. A test resumes a finished campaign and shows it creates no node and returns a stop_reason. A test shows resume calls create_campaign zero times and re-seals zero times. Every test passes under pytest-xdist.

System keeps the sandbox child's import allowlist in step with what the runtime can import, so a signal is refused at the guard for a module the runtime cannot import, instead of failing at execution with a wasted trial. - numpy is removed from AGENT_IMPORTS_ALLOWLIST and from _TRUSTED_IMPORT_ROOTS, because the evaluation runtime (the gVisor runtime root, and the evaluator's own environment) does not install numpy. A signal that imports numpy is now refused at the guard with the existing disallowed_import error, a deterministic refusal, in place of a runtime ImportError. - polars, pyarrow, contract and the standard-library modules the allowlist names remain, and a benign polars signal still scores. - A test asserts that every module named in AGENT_IMPORTS_ALLOWLIST is importable in the child's own interpreter, so the allowlist cannot drift from the runtime again. The test imports each name in a subprocess with the child's own -I flags and fails naming any that does not import. - No other behaviour of the child changes: the import guard, the builtins stripping, the result channel and the fail classes are unchanged.

System verifies the gVisor runtime root against its manifest before running agent code in it, so a partial or tampered root is refused rather than used. - GVisorSandbox reads <runtime_root>.manifest.json at construction and recomputes the tree digest the same way the provisioning script does — the sha256 of the sorted per-file sha256 sums of every file under the root — and compares it to the manifest's tree_sha256. - A missing manifest, malformed JSON, a missing tree_sha256, or a digest that does not match raises GVisorUnavailableError (code word isolation_required) naming the root and the mismatch. Construction succeeds only when the digest matches. - A trusted-root check env escape hatch is not added; the only way to run is a matching digest. The check reads files, never executes anything from the root. - deploy/gvisor/provision_runtime.sh is updated only if needed so the digest it writes is computed by the identical algorithm the sandbox recomputes (sorted per-file sha256 sums, hashed); the two must agree on a freshly provisioned root. - Tests build a small fake runtime root and manifest in a tmp dir (not the real 455 MB root): a matching digest constructs; a mutated file, a missing manifest and a bad tree_sha256 each raise. Tests do not require runsc for the digest checks (runsc resolution is stubbed or the check is exercised below the run path), and pass under xdist.

project_specification.integration_points: Each feature edits one existing source file in its own member plus a test file; test_campaign_resume.py is new and committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves. No new module, component, member or dependency. The run.sh operator verb and its 1Password template for a live campaign are an operator step, done by hand outside this spec.
project_specification.constraints: - resume_campaign never calls create_campaign or re-seals nulls; it continues an existing campaign and refuses an empty one. - Removing numpy must not break a polars-based signal; polars must not require numpy at import in the runtime. - The runtime-root digest check reads files only and never executes code from the root; there is no env var that bypasses it. - Do not edit the evaluator, nulloracle, ledger, discovery or policy-runtime members, the migrations, run.sh, the .env templates, claw-forge.yaml or docs/user-journeys/. - All existing workspace tests (tests/) and the orchestrator and signal-agent member suites stay green, and every new test passes under pytest-xdist.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1: campaign resume (feature 1), numpy allowlist (feature 2), and runtime-root verification (feature 3), in parallel.
